subject: dropping NAs out of an average

messages.author: 0c0915d54307a5d8
messages.subject: dropping NAs out of an average
parts:
I have a data frame (tadlengths) with five columns of tadpole lengths for a bunch of different treatments. I want to average the five lengths. I did this by:

meanlength = apply(tadlengths, 1, mean)

However, sometimes I only had four lengths, so there are NAs in those rows. I want to average the four lengths on those rows, but the code above gives me "NA" for those rows. I feel like there is a very, very, easy solution for this, but I can't figure it out!

Attached is the data file.

--

UC Davis Graduate Group in Ecology
Dr. Sharon Lawler's Lab

messages.author: 4742ff1f9fc5f9ca
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: dropping NAs out of an average
parts:
I think you should be able to add na.rm=T to the apply function.

meanlength = apply(tadlengths, 1, mean, na.rm=T)

-Matt

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: dropping NAs out of an average
parts:
By the way, using T instead of TRUE can be dangerous.  T, unlike TRUE can be re-defined.

For example, this would fail:

T = 0
